searchText: Just some feedback as someone who is using lido, the reason I don’t stake directly myself is due to the danger, complexity, and the deposit queue. Well that and when I tried to stake through eth pool they banned me. I know danger/risk is cited by many who are technically savy enough to stake but choose not to. Complexity I get. What is the perceived danger? Worried it’ll be hacked or stolen Also I don’t believe it’s compatible with ledger yet I believe Vitalik also said he doesn’t stake because it’s too risky 😂 Your validator key should be different from your withdraw key, and your withdraw key can be any Ethereum address IIUC. I understand the system But the unknown is scary? Plus ledger doesn’t support it which means my risk goes up If your validator key is hacked/stolen, the attacker can only make you take an illegal validator action, which has epsilon benefit to attacker and limited losses to you. While the reward to take that risk is just the lido fee Your withdraw address can be a ledger I believe, which is what matters. If so then that makes me feel better and makes it more likely I’ll stake The other issue would be I’d have 2 weeks without rewards when depositing When you give your stake to Lido, you are taking on all of the same risks, plus some more. You just avoid complexity. And couldn’t withdraw fast when needed Lido is divided among multiple parties though so I assume I’m risking 20% max not 100% If one goes down Similar to a mutual fund Been a while since I have looked at lido, but I believe there is no aggregate risk reduction. Your risk may be distributed a bit differently, but net risk I think is similar/the same. Lido has multiple operators I assume all of them can’t be hacked at once? There should be different withdrawal keys for each Sure, but all of those operators individually suffer the exact same set of risks. Also I assumed if lido is hacked you’d be willing to dao fork At least more likely than if my individual self was And I don't believe lido operator SS are KYCed, so there is no guarantee there are actually many Lido operators 100% against. I would exit Ethereum if the community bailed out Lido. Yeah but you must agree there’s a decent chance it’ll happen I think Ethereum would tank if so. It would be a strong signal that we have just recreated TradFi with too big too fail financial institutions. The problem with one entity being so big is you have to care about them No, you don't. We can and should let them fail. Anyway I’ve been looking at staking through blox Which just runs the validators for you but you keep the keys If it were possible (it isn't), I would push for bailing out individual validator failures and *not* large validator failures. But the deposit queue and illiquidity is what keeps me from doing so If they run the validator, then they have the validator keys. You can keep the withdraw keys though. “Users running a validator using Blox Staking keep complete control over their private keys, as in a solo setup. The value-add of running a validator using Blox is that stakers can enjoy the security of an at-home validator without the hassle of updating, maintaining, and defending against slashing on one’s own.” They advertise as the only ones to support it It is literally impossible to operate a validator without the validator keys. Either they mean you keep your withdraw keys, or they are doing something silly like relying on SGX for validator key security. Probably SGX Btw, so a validator can be withdrawn to any wallet? Not just the wallet that staked? If so, then that increases my fear 10x. I'd feel so much safer if it could only go back into my ledger. I believe they run the beacon node and you run the validator client. So you do indeed have your own keys. Someone does it that way anyway - I think it was Blox.
